segmentation.text: outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle, whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
an unobstructed width of the highway
shall be left for the free passage of other vehicles
a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway: "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders"; x is upon it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed by id; 'whether attended or unattended' excludes no member.

The standing vehicles 'in every event' are those of the first clause, upon the paved or main-traveled part: the st.roadway ("the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder"), overlapped by x's footprint (rel.occupies).

A width of the highway opposite the vehicle is a lane beside it: a st.lane ("a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles") on the same highway (st.on_way, st.highway) whose ground distance from x's body (st.region_geometry) is at most the beside reach, so that a lane segment far along the way is not read, and that x's footprint does not overlap (rel.occupies). Unobstructed: no other halted road user beside x occupies it.

'a standing vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not") is x halted (drv.motion.halted, kin.speed at or below the resolution); its purpose is not observable (observable_reading purpose). Opposite it is the stretch alongside its body: another halted road user is opposite where their footprints overlap along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive), a projection, 'not' a contact or a distance.

A vehicle disabled on the roadway is read through its nearest observables, as in the first obligation of this line: engine or motor not running (kin.engine_running: "so that propulsion is available", false) with hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard: "both indicators flashing together"), while it occupies the roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway). kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in' for motion or a halt; the gap records that the disability itself has no atom.

operationalizations.standard: an unobstructed width left for the free passage of other vehicles
operationalizations.convention: Free-passage convention: the width left for passage is a lane beside the standing vehicle, not overlapped by it and not taken by another halted road user alongside it, whose measured width (st.lane_width) is at least a design passenger-car width plus lateral clearance.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside a business district or a residence district declared for the map or the trace.

applicability: x carries ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; at the observation x is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) with its footprint overlapping a st.roadway of a st.highway h (rel.occupies, st.on_way); asm.within_business_or_residence_district does not hold; and x is not disabled there: not (kin.engine_running false and sig.hazard on).
obligation: Some st.lane L on h (st.on_way(L, h)) that x's footprint does not overlap, within p.opposite_lane_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry distance), has st.lane_width at least p.free_passage_width, and no road user other than x that is halted (drv.motion.halted with p.speed_resolution) and overlaps x along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive) occupies L.

narrowings.why: 'an unobstructed width of the highway' is read as a whole lane beside the vehicle, free of halted road users alongside it; a part-lane, a shoulder, or an obstruction that is not a road user (st.obstruction) is not counted.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a rural two-lane highway x (ru.motor_vehicle) halts in one lane while another vehicle halts in the other lane alongside it (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive): no lane beside x is free.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x halts in one lane of a rural two-lane highway; the other lane, within p.opposite_lane_reach, has st.lane_width above p.free_passage_width and no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x drives along the rural roadway without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x halts in one lane of a rural two-lane highway with the other lane empty, but the source does not observe lane widths.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x halts with its engine not running and its hazard lamps flashing: the disabled-vehicle exception applies.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.free_passage_width
param_proposals.convention: Free-passage width: the smallest width of an unoccupied lane beside a standing vehicle that lets another vehicle pass; a design passenger-car width plus lateral clearance.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book design-vehicle widths and lane widths

param_proposals.name: p.opposite_lane_reach
param_proposals.convention: Beside reach: the largest ground distance from a standing vehicle's body to a lane within which the lane counts as opposite the vehicle; covers the lateral gap between the body and the next lane's edge.

gaps.proposal: `ru.disabled` | a vehicle that cannot proceed under its own power, by a mechanical failure, crash damage or a flat tyre, as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** a vehicle parked with its engine off, or one showing hazard lamps | general — decides whether moving the vehicle off the roadway can be carried out, which the disabled-vehicle exception turns on
